question: What is an SCSS partial?
shortAnswer: A file named _name.scss intended to be loaded by other files, not compiled standalone.
detailedAnswer: Partials organize code. With modern toolchains, entrypoints @use partials explicitly.

question: @use vs @import for partials — why migrate?
shortAnswer: @use loads once, namespaces members, and enables configured modules; @import is deprecated and global.
detailedAnswer: Migration is a senior practical topic. Plan namespaces and @forward facades.
interviewTip: Mention load-once and namespacing as the key wins.

question: What does @forward do?
shortAnswer: Re-exports members from a module as part of your package's public API.
detailedAnswer: Build index facades: @forward 'tokens'; @forward 'mixins'. Hide internals with show/hide.

question: How do you configure a module with @use ... with?
shortAnswer: Pass overrides to !default variables when loading: @use 'theme' with ($brand: #123).
detailedAnswer: Enables per-app theming without globals. Order matters — configure at first load.

question: Circular dependency between partials — symptoms?
shortAnswer: Load errors or surprising incomplete members; often tokens ↔ mixins cycles.
detailedAnswer: Extract a lower-level tokens module. Dependency direction: tokens → tools → components.

question: Folder structure for scalable SCSS partials?
shortAnswer: tokens/, tools/ (mixins/functions), base/, components/, pages/ — with a single entry main.scss.
detailedAnswer: Align with ITCSS or similar. Keep component partials isolated. Avoid pages importing each other.

question: Scenario: CSS duplication after splitting partials.
shortAnswer: Same mixin included via multiple component paths is OK (declarations duplicate) vs accidental double load of side-effect files.
detailedAnswer: Prefer side-effect-free modules. Put global resets only in base entry once.

question: Should partials emit CSS when loaded?
shortAnswer: Prefer silent modules (only variables/mixins/functions) vs components that emit; control emission from entrypoints.
detailedAnswer: Silent modules compose better. Component partials emit once when used.

question: Debugging: styles missing because partial not used.
shortAnswer: Entrypoint forgot @use/@forward; or wrong path; or build includes only main.
detailedAnswer: Treat main.scss as the manifest. CI compile check helps.

question: How do Sass load paths help monorepos?
shortAnswer: Include shared package paths so @use 'design-system/tokens' resolves without brittle relatives.
detailedAnswer: Configure in bundler/sass options. Version the design system package.

question: Partials vs CSS modules co-existence?
shortAnswer: SCSS partials for global tokens/tools; CSS modules for component-scoped class hashes.
detailedAnswer: Define boundaries clearly. Don't @use heavy globals into every CSS module carelessly.

question: Naming conventions for partials?
shortAnswer: _tokens.scss, _mixins.scss, component names matching UI; avoid vague _helpers2.
detailedAnswer: Consistency beats cleverness. Index files for folders via @forward.

question: Lead: migrate a 10-year @import codebase to @use/@forward.
shortAnswer: Incremental facades, compatibility layers, namespace as you go, and ban new @import in lint.
detailedAnswer: Track compile warnings. Don't big-bang without visual regression tests.

question: What belongs in a public SCSS package entrypoint?
shortAnswer: Forwarded tokens, mixins, functions — not private experimental partials.
detailedAnswer: Semantic versioning for removed forwards. Document peer Sass version.
